title: Charging performance shortfall at low ambient temperature
engineering_question: Charging performance is worse than expected under one environmental condition. Is this a defect, a specification gap, or expected behaviour?
one_liner: Determine whether the observed charging performance constitutes a non-conformance.
initial_input: DC charge time from 10 to 80 percent state of charge measured at 8 degC ambient exceeds the reference-condition target by 9 to 14 minutes across three vehicles.
expected_impacted_domains: Charging strategy and current limit derivation
Requirement completeness across the environmental envelope
expected_reasoning_paths: TR-007 passes at the reference condition and TR-006 is inconclusive at low ambient, so the vehicle is not demonstrably non-conforming
The real finding is that REQ-040 defines a target only at the reference condition, so no low ambient obligation exists to fail against
This is a requirements completeness gap that should be raised as a specification action rather than a defect
known_unknowns: No battery preconditioning strategy is represented in the environment
Competitive benchmark charge times are not available
data_classification: SIMULATED ENTERPRISE ARTEFACT - not OEM, customer or proprietary data
